prose: A developer laid off from Meta argues heavy AI coding makes fragile codebases. He generated at least 90% of his code with AI there and now 100%, but saw peers merge brittle code, such as mouseover effects done in JavaScript instead of CSS :hover. AI solves what fits its context window and misses long-term issues. He lists four failure modes, starting with simplistic tests that cover trivial getters or only already-covered cases. The author says the article was written by a human.
highlights: AI code is brittle beyond its context window
Tests are shallow and leave hidden gaps
Four ways AI creates fragile SaaS code
